messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall (devon). Elevated 5xx/timeouts from private inference gateway in us-west-2 affecting VPC deployments. Alert: private-gateway-5xx-rate > 5% for 3m.
ashley: seeing a ton of 504s in the customer-facing private endpoints since ~09:12 UTC. Multiple customers reporting inference timeouts, dashboards show spike in gateway 504 and backend timeouts.
devon: ack, taking this. Which path — dedicated NAT, peering, or firewall? any correlation with recent deploys?
ashley: no deploys in the last hour. Errors are only for private/vpc routes (hosted customers OK). CPU on gateway nodes looks normal, but egress errors to model-serving pods show TCP reset/timeout.
leah: checking cloudwatch for NAT and peering metrics... grabbing counters.
leah: nat-gateway-ephemeral-ports-used trending to 98%, conntrack entries near capacity on transit appliance. Cloudwatch: SNATPortUtilization peak 96% at 09:14.
mike: security-group rules look unchanged. No deny rules that would explain it. Peering route tables stable.
devon: sounds like ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT/transit path causing new outbound connections to fail -> 5xx gateway. Good catch leah. Can you paste the conntrack snapshot?
leah: pasting output snippet from transit appliance (sanitized):
```
# conntrack -S
entries 120450
```
leah: sysctl shows nf_conntrack_max=131072 and current entries ~120k. That's dangerously close.
devon: yep that's the problem. When conntrack saturates, new sessions get dropped -> backend timeouts/504s. We need immediate mitigation: reduce load on that NAT, roll traffic to alternate egress, and increase conntrack limits as hotfix.
customer_ops: several enterprise customers are impacted (cust-a, cust-b). Customer success is on a call but asking for ETA and mitigation steps.
jonas: I'm on standby to take handoff if needed.
devon: mitigation plan (live): 1) Failover affected subnets to secondary NAT gateway (immediate). 2) Bump nf_conntrack_max and ephemeral port range on transit appliance(s) as temporary patch. 3) Investigate root cause: sudden connection churn (likely workload change or retry storm). 4) Postmortem and capacity increase.
devon: executing failover now, replacing route on rtb-private-apps to nat-secondary. Command: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-PRIVATEAPP --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-SECONDARY` (already applied, awaiting propagation).
leah: route table replace reported success, propagation confirmed in 15s. Monitoring egress errors...
mike: I'm preparing a quick patch to bump conntrack on transit appliances. Command to run on the appliance: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and bump port range: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"`. Will run on two active appliances in the next 30s.
devon: do it on one, monitor for regressions, then second. Also apply `echo 524288 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` for persistence (but we won't persist during incident).
leah: conntrack max bumped to 524288 on appliance-1. Entries now 120k -> should accept new connections. Monitoring metrics.
devon: checking gateway dashboards: 5xx rate dropping from ~8% to 1.2% post-failover and conntrack bump. Latency back to baseline on private gateway.
customer_ops: notified customers that we have failed over egress and applied hotfix. ETA communicated as ~10-15m. They want a writeup for the call.
ashley: thanks team. Can we confirm no packet drops in peering? tcpdump on gateway shows completed 3-way handshakes now.
mike: tcpdump snippet: `SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK` flows returning. No RST flood.
devon: moving to containment -> patching transit appliances with new conntrack limits across fleet, scheduling NAT capacity increase. We'll also add alerting on conntrack supply and SNATPortUtilization at lower thresholds.
jonas: taking 3-11 shift. Handing off next steps: 1) finalize fleet-wide sysctl change, make config change in our Ansible/packer templates. 2) Provision extra NAT capacity (scale up or add nat-eip). 3) Run replay load test to validate. 4) Postmortem owners: ashley (customer impact + comms), devon (network root cause + remediation), leah (metrics + dashboarding).
devon: noted. I'll create a follow-up ticket and link to this thread. Ticket will include commands run, timestamps, affected customers, and suggested infra changes.
incident-bot: incident status updated -> mitigated. Reduced error rates observed and traffic routed to secondary NAT.
customer_ops: customers acknowledged mitigation, will wait for postmortem. One customer asked for any possible data loss? We confirmed no inference results lost, just timeouts/retries.
leah: final metrics snapshot: private-gateway-5xx reduced to 0.9% at 09:36 UTC, SNATPortUtilization back to <20% after failover.
jonas: I'm oncall now, will monitor for 2h and then close if stable.
devon: thanks everyone. Post-incident action items assigned and priorities set to P1 for NAT capacity.
ashley: closing loop with customers and ops. Great work. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident closed by devon at 2356789140.
